threads.body: This test only verifies no spans exist after instrument+uninstrument, but it never invokes an async Responses call to prove the async patch was actually removed. Consider invoking `async_openai_client.responses.create(...)` after `uninstrument()` (within a cassette) and asserting that still no spans are produced, which would actually exercise the new `AsyncResponses.create` unwrap path added in this PR.

threads.body: `REASONING_MODEL = \"gpt-5.4\"` is not a real OpenAI model name. While the test is replayed from a recorded VCR cassette so it currently passes, using a non-existent model identifier is misleading and could confuse maintainers re-recording cassettes. Consider using a real reasoning-capable model such as `\"o1-mini\"` or `\"gpt-5\"` and re-recording the cassette.

threads.body: The error-injecting delegate is defined inside the test function and uses a counter to fire on the second iteration. Naming the threshold via a named constant (e.g. `ERROR_AFTER_EVENTS = 1`) or extracting the helper class to module scope would make the intent clearer and improve reuse for similar future tests.
